text:
Leaves gently drift to the ground as birds of all colors fly above and away from the source of a rhythmic pounding that shakes the colossal trees to their 
roots. The Traveler grips their spear tightly, fearing some imminent natural calamity. A resounding crack and crash is heard through the woods, and the 
pounding stops, replaced by a hushed silence and the quickened breath of the Traveler.
Venturing onward, stepping lightly over branch and leaf, the forest around them eerily silent but for the sound of wet crunching. Staying low to the 
ground, the Traveler steps into a clearing that ends in a steep hill of stone and grass, shafts of sunlight twinkle with the dust and pollen that rises off the 
dark green foliage. It is peaceful for a moment, until, incomprehensibly, the hill turns.
Taking a step back in utter shock, a porcine head as large as the Traveler is tall, looks to peer at the startled biped. Thick mouldering tree pulp falling from 
yellowed teeth, a large wet nose sniffing the air, before it grumbles deeply and lowers its massive head back to chew upon the old fallen tree. Breathing out 
the longest, quietest sigh of relief, the Traveler gently settles onto an old stump, pulls out their journal and begins to sketch the enormous beast.
As one of the few colossal mega-fauna on Sol'Kesh, and an extreme example of island gigantism, this massive boar absolutely dominates 
the Wealdwoods that it calls home. Rarely do any of their kind reach these massive sizes, often dying to infection or injury before 
entering the eighth or ninth decade of their long life cycle,  when they grow to reach passed the tree line, their limbs creaking and eyes 
blinded by countless ailments. Often preceded by the sound of heavy resounding foot falls and the crash of rotten branches falling to 
the ground, the beast is heard long before its shaggy form is seen, slowly pushing through the trees like a natural disaster. Unhurried 
as it knows little can stand against its thorned hide and terrible strength. The creature’s incredibly sensitive nose leads them through 
dozens of miles of their territory, searching for the festering remains of the dead, rich fungus clusters that riddle the roots and logs, 
and when famished, the soft wood of dead trees, as the beast can digest nearly anything. While this slow moving beast exudes a calm 
passive demeanor, when confronted by aggressive predators, like the horned sacrissian or mindlessly voracious nicalliath, it won't 
hesitate to prove its position as apex, and will batter the contenders to a crushed ruin with its tusks and immense size. The most 
legendary battles within the Wealdwoods often begin by mistake, when the jhotus inadvertently steps on a waiting korrask and has to 
violently rip the insect out of the earth to end the ensuing struggle. Though little can slay this beast, when they do eventually perish, 
their disappearance may lead to an unhealthy rise in rot and fungal decay within the Wealdwoods they called home.
Balance is the key to any ecosystem, supporting something as large as the jhotus, allowing it to grow without exhausting what it could 
eat, means that the species must greatly benefit its environment in kind, and despite its apparent destructive habits, the jhotus does 
just that.
Not all Wealdwoods can support families of jhotus, though they may roam alone, they need wide swaths of territory to feast and mate 
to still maintain a healthy genetic diversity. The Tanglewood, like a vast sea of trees, harbors the most jhotus, with more than enough 
old groves and sunken swamps to offer the massive beasts the decay they hunger for. The colder climate of the Last Bloom woods, with 
its syrup laden trees hosts a smaller, but no less dominating group. Lastly, the Greenmoot, a young forest that offers little of the soft 
rotten woods that the giant swine prefers, instead many of the jhotus that call these greener forests home, will venture up to the white 
Rhaen rapids, dipping their heads into the cold water and feasting on sea grasses and any unfortunate fish that mistakes their gaping 
maws for a cave.
Their presence within a forest, while overwhelmingly destructive in appearance, is not just a protective bulwark to hold back more 
aggressive predators, but one of cultivation. By feasting on the oldest of trees, felling them years before weather would do the same, 
allows new growth to take root earlier, and rise to the sunlight above. With the ability to digest nearly anything; rotten bones, thick 
festering pits of fungus and befouled larvae-infested stumps, all are greedily eaten up by the voracious swine. This trophic level of 
detritivore is often claimed by the smallest of creatures, flies, worms and other pests, but none can match the amount of rot an adult 
jhotus can clear out. When a new swath of territory is claimed by a family of these beasts, within a few seasons there's a noticeable 
change in the forest. Impenetrable ground cover is pushed aside to leave wide hunting trails from the beasts relentless tread, and a 
blossoming growth of low level bushes, their healthy bright leaves attracting all manner of herbivores. And lastly, though sometimes 
best left unsaid, its enormous piles of excrement fertilize the often nutrient-poor soil of the forest, helping the large trees that the apex 
predator calls home to grow tall, further expanding the forest and sheltering more beasts within its boughs.
For those stepping into the Wealdwoods that are patrolled by families of jhotus, it is far from the tranquility of newly growing life. 
While generally calm, they are still beasts, and when confronted by anything that they deem a threat, or even a nuisance, they will not 
forgo the use of their bulk to prove their dominance. Nothing on the island, beyond the sheer cliffs of the Splitspine can halt the charge 
of a furious jhotus, when enraged, trees hundreds of feet high will still break from the impact of its enormous shoulders, boulders will 
crack, and anything else foolish enough to stand in its way. Only when its heaving breath does not catch the invader's scent any longer 
will it finally settle back into a peaceful journey, munching through its forest.
